correctness.rationale: Exact bijection between deletion-correcting codes and binary feasible solutions is proved: all 495 common one-deletion-output cliques are constrained. The 143-code construction is rigorously shown by mod-five relabeling and independently pair-checked over 10,153 pairs. The included checker.py globally optimizes the complete 715-variable clique MILP at objective 143 with dual bound -142.99999999999955 and zero MIP gap. The separately constructed checker_edges.py uses 4,950 pair inequalities and independently globally optimizes at 143 with dual bound -142.99999999999983. Both programs were executed successfully from their package paths. The proof is computational, dependent on soundness of HiGHS branch-and-bound, without an independently checkable exact rational unsatisfiability proof.

value.rationale: A natural complete exact optimum, at the first blocklength missing from the source paper’s explicit quinary table, gives a concrete new instance of its named open Conjecture 21. It tests whether the prime-field syndrome construction remains unrestricted-optimal, with relevance to unordered-deletion coding benchmarks. Not claimed to solve the infinite conjecture.
